BiblicalUsage: Pelos is clay. Jesus spat on the ground, made clay of the spittle, and anointed the blind man's eyes, and the man washed and received his sight. Paul asks whether the potter has no power over the clay, to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that I am the clay and God is the potter: He shapes me as He wills, and my part is to yield to His hands. Jesus used clay to open blind eyes, and Paul used it to answer every complaint against God's sovereignty. I hold that the vessel has no right to argue with the potter — but the potter's hands are good hands, and the clay is safe in them.
